headline: Highest risk is low: no shared runtime surfaces are documented, so prompt injection, leakage, and capability conflict are not evidenced for this pair.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Neither profile documents a shared communication channel, writable filesystem, clipboard, MCP, or stdin/stdout bridge. Dagster is non-runnable with no IO surfaces, and data-engineering-zoomcamp also shows no IO surfaces or runtime capabilities. Without a bridge, prompt injection between them is not plausible.
conditions: IF either agent is connected to a shared clipboard, filesystem, or MCP server, reassess as non-none.
IF an orchestrator copies one agent's text directly into the other, prompt injection becomes possible.
mitigations: Keep the agents in separate workspaces.
Disable any copy-paste automation between them.
Do not mount a shared MCP server or message queue.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging if a bridge is later introduced.

B_data_leakage.rationale: No data classes are listed for either agent, and both profiles show no network egress. Dagster has no filesystem read/write surfaces, while data-engineering-zoomcamp exposes no IO surfaces at all. With no documented shared workspace or outbound channel, there is no plausible leakage path in the profiles provided.
conditions: IF either agent is given access to sensitive files or a shared workspace, leakage risk must be re-evaluated.
IF either agent gains outbound network access, data exfiltration risk increases.
mitigations: Keep sensitive files out of both agents' environments.
Avoid shared folders or synced drives.
Confirm outbound network remains disabled.
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation at the OS level.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Capability overlap is absent: Dagster cannot write the filesystem, modify git state, or spawn subprocesses, and the zoomcamp profile exposes no write or concurrency capabilities. With no shared mutable resource or locking gap documented, there is no capability conflict pathway.
conditions: IF either profile is updated to write the same directory or git repo, conflict risk becomes non-none.
IF an orchestrator grants shared mutable access, reassess for write contention.
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only.
Do not point them at the same git repository.
Avoid shared databases or buckets.
requires-engineering: add explicit locking before any shared writes.

D_cascading_error.rationale: There is no documented pipeline where Dagster's output becomes authoritative input for data-engineering-zoomcamp, and neither profile shows downstream action-taking authority. The zoomcamp profile is a course/repo, not an autonomous executor, so the usual A-to-B automation cascade is not evidenced.
conditions: IF an orchestrator starts feeding Dagster outputs into an automated action agent, reassess.
IF the zoomcamp repo is wrapped in a tool that executes instructions, cascading error risk changes.
mitigations: Require human review before acting on generated outputs.
Do not auto-commit or auto-send based on one agent's text.
Keep the course repo as reference material only.
requires-engineering: add verification gates before any downstream action.

E_compliance.rationale: No sensitive data classes, residency constraints, certifications, or retention policies are documented for either agent. Because the profiles do not show PHI, EU PII, or regulated-data handling, there is no compliance mismatch to score from the available evidence.
conditions: IF either agent is later assigned regulated data, compliance must be re-scored.
IF residency or retention requirements are introduced, reassess for mismatch.
mitigations: Document data classes before deployment.
Avoid regulated data until policies are explicit.
Review retention settings if any storage is added.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for regulated datasets.
